types.label: AI Product
types.description: A complete, user-facing solution with its own interface, defined end users and an ongoing roadmap, used directly by staff as a tool in their daily work (e.g. AI dictation app).

types.label: AI System
types.description: An AI capability embedded within existing enterprise systems or workflows (such as the HIS or EMR) that operates largely in the background to automate or optimise a process (e.g. OPD scheduling optimisation).

types.label: AI Service
types.description: An AI capability delivered on demand to a specific team or to other systems, either as an analytical service producing outputs for a business function or as a reusable API (e.g. CPG compliance scoring for the audit team).

phases.label: Idea
phases.description: A use case has been proposed and logged in the portfolio but not yet assessed.

phases.label: Assessment
phases.description: Evaluating feasibility, business value, data availability, clinical and privacy risk, and cost to decide whether to proceed.

phases.label: Not Started
phases.description: Approved and prioritised, but delivery work has not yet begun.

phases.label: Planning
phases.description: Defining scope, business case, success KPIs, stakeholders, resources and timeline.

phases.label: Data Preparation
phases.description: Securing data access and privacy approvals, then extracting, cleaning and labelling the data needed to build the solution.

phases.label: Development
phases.description: Building the solution, including model development, integration and interface work.

phases.label: Evaluation
phases.description: Technical and clinical validation against agreed accuracy, safety and performance criteria, including clinical governance review where applicable.

phases.label: UAT
phases.description: End users test the solution in realistic scenarios to confirm it meets business needs.

phases.label: Pilot
phases.description: Limited live use in one department or hospital to confirm real-world performance, adoption and benefits before wider rollout.

phases.label: Deployment
phases.description: Releasing the solution to production, including go-live preparation, training and rollout.

phases.label: Scale-up
phases.description: Extending the solution to additional departments, hospitals or user groups after a successful pilot or initial deployment.

phases.label: Live
phases.description: In production use under early-life monitoring to stabilise performance and track benefits.

phases.label: Benefits Review
phases.description: Formal post-implementation review comparing actual results with the expected KPIs in the business case.

phases.label: Support
phases.description: Handed over to business-as-usual, with ongoing maintenance, monitoring of model performance and drift, and periodic review.

phases.label: Enhancement
phases.description: A new improvement cycle on a live solution, such as added features, model retraining or expanded scope.

phases.label: On Hold
phases.description: Formally paused by decision of the sponsor or steering committee, pending a resolution, priority or resource change.

phases.label: Cancelled
phases.description: Formally stopped before completion because it is no longer viable, valuable or a priority.

phases.label: Retired
phases.description: A previously live solution that has been decommissioned or replaced and is no longer in use.

statuses.label: On Track
statuses.description: Progressing according to the planned scope, timeline and resources, with no significant issues.

statuses.label: At Risk
statuses.description: Risks or issues have been identified that may affect scope, timeline or quality if not addressed; corrective action is needed.

statuses.label: Delayed
statuses.description: Behind the original schedule, but the cause is understood and a revised date has been agreed.

statuses.label: Off Track
statuses.description: Significantly deviating from plan on timeline, budget, scope or quality; a recovery plan and sponsor attention are required.

statuses.label: Blocked
statuses.description: Progress has stopped due to a dependency or issue the team cannot resolve on its own and requires escalation.

statuses.label: Pending Decision
statuses.description: Waiting for an approval or decision from the sponsor, a committee or governance body before work can continue.

statuses.label: Under Review
statuses.description: The project is being reassessed (for example a health check, scope change or re-prioritisation) and its direction may change.

statuses.label: Not Reported
statuses.description: No status update has been submitted within the required reporting period.

statuses.label: Not Applicable
statuses.description: Status tracking does not apply in the current phase (e.g. Idea, Cancelled or Retired).

statuses.label: Done
statuses.description: All objectives for the current phase or the project have been achieved and formally accepted.

domains.label: 1. Clinical Informatics
domains.description: The technology behind patient care, including the hospital information system (HIS), electronic medical records, clinical data accuracy, and how doctors and nurses use digital tools in daily work.

domains.label: 2. Clinical Governance
domains.description: The quality and safety of patient care, including clinical policies, accreditation (such as JCI and GAHAR), incident reporting, audits, infection control, and clinical outcome KPIs.

domains.label: 3. Medical Coding and Pricing
domains.description: Turning diagnoses and procedures into standard codes (ICD and CPT), setting service prices and packages, and making sure claims to insurers and contracted companies are accurate and get paid.

domains.label: 4. Human Resources
domains.description: The workforce, including hiring doctors, nurses and staff, credentialing, payroll, performance management, retention, and staffing levels across the branches.

domains.label: 5. Academy and L&D
domains.description: Staff training and development, including clinical and non-clinical courses, onboarding, CME for doctors, nursing programs, certifications, and building future leaders.

domains.label: 6. Pharmacy
domains.description: Everything about medicines, including the formulary, drug stock, dispensing, medication safety, controlled drugs, and pharmacy revenue.

domains.label: 7. Supply Chain
domains.description: Getting the right items at the right cost, including procurement, vendor management, warehouses and inventory, and the availability of medical supplies and equipment.

domains.label: 8. Finance
domains.description: The company’s financial health, including revenue by hospital and department, costs, budgets, cash collection, insurance receivables, profitability, and financial reporting.

domains.label: 9. Construction
domains.description: New buildings and expansions, such as the AOH hospital project. This covers project timelines, budgets, contractors, engineering packages, and long-lead equipment.

req_categories.label: Functional
req_categories.description: What the solution does: a feature, capability or behaviour visible to users or other systems.

req_categories.label: Non-Functional
req_categories.description: How well the solution does it: quality attributes such as speed, security, privacy, reliability and cost.

nfr_areas.label: Performance
nfr_areas.description: Response time, processing time and throughput targets.

nfr_areas.label: Scalability
nfr_areas.description: Number of concurrent users, sessions or records the solution must handle.

nfr_areas.label: Availability & Reliability
nfr_areas.description: Uptime, failover, retries, recovery and protection against data loss.

nfr_areas.label: Security
nfr_areas.description: Authentication, access control, secrets management and security testing.

nfr_areas.label: Privacy & Data Protection
nfr_areas.description: Handling of patient and personal data, anonymisation and data minimisation.

nfr_areas.label: Accuracy & Clinical Safety
nfr_areas.description: Correctness of AI output, no invented content, clinical validation and safety checks.

nfr_areas.label: Data Integrity
nfr_areas.description: Completeness, freshness and consistency of stored and processed data.

nfr_areas.label: Usability
nfr_areas.description: Ease of use, language support and user workflow.

nfr_areas.label: Interoperability & Integration
nfr_areas.description: Integration with HIS, data warehouse, SharePoint, Teams and other systems.

nfr_areas.label: Compliance & Regulatory
nfr_areas.description: Data residency, regulatory and internal compliance approvals.

nfr_areas.label: Auditability & Observability
nfr_areas.description: Audit trails, logging, monitoring and usage reporting.

nfr_areas.label: Maintainability & Operability
nfr_areas.description: Configuration, release control, ease of change and continuous improvement.

nfr_areas.label: Cost Efficiency
nfr_areas.description: AI and infrastructure cost targets and cost tracking.

nfr_areas.label: Platform & Hosting
nfr_areas.description: Required platform, cloud provider and AI model providers.

nfr_areas.label: Scope & Constraints
nfr_areas.description: Agreed boundaries and limitations of the solution.

request_types.label: Baseline
request_types.description: An existing capability of the current live or retired version, recorded for reference.

request_types.label: New Project
request_types.description: A requirement for a solution that does not exist yet.

request_types.label: New Version
request_types.description: A requirement delivered as part of a major new version of an existing solution.

request_types.label: BR / CR
request_types.description: A business request or change request on an existing solution.

req_priorities.label: Critical
req_priorities.description: Essential for go-live; the release cannot proceed without it, or it addresses a patient-safety, legal or security risk.

req_priorities.label: High
req_priorities.description: Important for business value; expected in the current release.

req_priorities.label: Medium
req_priorities.description: Useful improvement; delivered if time and capacity allow, otherwise in the next release.

req_priorities.label: Low
req_priorities.description: Nice to have; can be deferred without significant impact.

req_statuses.label: Proposed
req_statuses.description: Raised but not yet reviewed or agreed.

req_statuses.label: Approved
req_statuses.description: Agreed by the business owner and planned for delivery.

req_statuses.label: Implemented
req_statuses.description: Built and available, awaiting or undergoing testing.

req_statuses.label: Verified
req_statuses.description: Tested and accepted (e.g. UAT, load or security test passed).
